reviews.comment: He's not bad, but the lectures were rather uninteresting (he practically just recites the textbook), but does give visuals which aren't too bad.  Homeworks and tests often have a few very tough questions but he curves the class very nicely subsequently.  Overall, nothing in the class really stands out as particularly bad or good.

Professor Liu will provide all the resources you need to be able to obtain an A in his class. Just read through the lecture notes(you can skip the proofs) and practice the quizzes/hws(especially the quizzes) and you should be able to do well in the class. His lectures can be tedious, but his notes were very helpful. He also gives a nice curve.

In my opinion the lectures weren't too useful so I didn't attend many. You are better off learning the content elsewhere. I just studied off of homeworks and did amazing on every quiz and test since there are no trick questions. Perfect professor if you want to get a good grade since he curves generously.

Nice guy, focused on a very theoretical linear algebra, if you don't like proofs probably avoid. Final had 25 true/false questions which was strange for a math test. Overall not a bad time but not a great time

Dr. Liu is very intelligent, yet teaches Linear Algebra primarily on a proof-based level. I recommend doing the homework ahead of his lectures in order to gain a better understanding on his examples. Overall, a good professor for LinAlg.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria
